items.title: The Strange Story of America’s First “Alien Abduction”
items.author: Weird History
items.content:
<article>During a late-night drive through rural New Hampshire in 1961, Barney and Betty Hill reported a terrifying encounter with a UFO that would change their lives forever. Since then, their story remains one of the most famous and controversial alien abduction cases in history. From unexplained missing time and hypnotic regression to eerie eyewitness testimony, the Hills' account helped shape modern beliefs about extraterrestrials, UFO sightings, and even the mysteries surrounding Area 51. But were they telling the truth, or did something else happen that night?

In this episode of Weird History Presents: Graveyard Shift, we explore the shocking details behind America's first widely publicized alien abduction case, the evidence that still fuels debate decades later, and why the Barney and Betty Hill story continues to captivate believers and skeptics alike.

items.author: Weird History
items.content:
<article>New Jersey's Action Park, the world's most infamous water park, closed its doors in 1996. It eventually reopened as Mountain Creek Waterpark, but in 2014 the son of the original owner brought back the legendary Action Park name. His goal was simple: recreate the thrill that made the original park famous, just without the injuries, lawsuits, and deadly reputation. But reviving America's most dangerous amusement park proved far more complicated than anyone expected.

LAST DAYS is Weird History’s prestige format series focusing on final chapters, deaths, downfalls and conclusions. items.title: How H.H. Holmes Became America’s First Serial Killer
items.author: Weird History
items.content:
<article>Long before he was hanged in 1896 for murdering his business partner, Herman Webster Mudgett, better known as Dr. Henry Howard Holmes, had built a reputation for fraud, deception, and violence. He also built an infamous "Murder Castle" in Chicago, a labyrinthine building allegedly designed to lure and kill travelers attending the 1893 World's Fair. Historians have confirmed at least nine victims, but many believe the true death toll may have been far, far higher.

On this episode of Weird History Presents: Graveyard Shift we separate the historical record from the sensational rumors surrounding H. H. Holmes, exploring the crimes, scams, and enduring mysteries that turned him into one of history's most notorious figures.
